caseEdges.label: E01
caseEdges.meaning: Experimental Study of the Triplet Synchronization of Coupled Nonidentical Mechanical Metronomes
caseEdges.support: Coupled nonidentical metronomes exhibit a collective triplet synchronization relation even where individual pairs are asynchronous.
caseEdges.supplied: Metronomes, their energy supply, and mechanical coupling already exist.
caseEdges.limit: Collective coordination need not mean every oscillator has one identical frequency or phase. This does not demonstrate the creation of the oscillators.
caseEdges.locator: 06_evidence_catalog.md E01; original-paper location as reported there
caseEdges.readDepth: Source-reported 2026-10-02: Publisher HTML, including experimental description. Not a fresh website paper audit.

caseEdges.label: E02
caseEdges.meaning: Controlling the motion of multiple objects on a Chladni plate
caseEdges.support: Plate vibrations can transport particles; the study uses controlled sequences of excitation to manipulate multiple objects.
caseEdges.supplied: A manufactured plate, particles, actuator, camera and control algorithm are provided.
caseEdges.limit: Distinguish ordinary nodal accumulation from the paper’s actively controlled manipulation. Neither establishes autonomous particle-to-field feedback or reproduction.
caseEdges.locator: 06_evidence_catalog.md E02; original-paper location as reported there
caseEdges.readDepth: Source-reported 2026-10-02: Publisher HTML and author-institution abstract. Supplementary videos linked on the paper page were not watched. Not a fresh website paper audit.

caseEdges.label: E03
caseEdges.meaning: Independent trapping and manipulation of microparticles using dexterous acoustic tweezers
caseEdges.support: A phased ultrasonic array independently traps and manipulates microparticles; reported examples include 45 and 90 micrometre spheres.
caseEdges.supplied: An engineered transducer array, liquid medium and pre-existing particles are required.
caseEdges.limit: This particular experiment supports microscale manipulation, not a claim of nanoscale performance or a universal size–frequency law.
caseEdges.locator: 06_evidence_catalog.md E03; original-paper location as reported there
caseEdges.readDepth: Source-reported 2026-10-02: Author-institution records and original-paper abstract; not a full methods or data audit. Not a fresh website paper audit.

caseEdges.label: E04
caseEdges.meaning: Noise-induced spatial periodicity in excitable chemical media
caseEdges.support: Numerical excitable-chemical-media dynamics show an intermediate noise regime with enhanced spatial periodicity.
caseEdges.supplied: An Oregonator-type reaction model, diffusion, parameter choices and noisy forcing are specified.
caseEdges.limit: This is a numerical result, not a laboratory observation of the primordial background. Noise acts through existing nonlinear dynamics.
caseEdges.locator: 06_evidence_catalog.md E04; original-paper location as reported there
caseEdges.readDepth: Source-reported 2026-10-02: Primary publisher record and abstract; equations and simulation data not independently reproduced. Not a fresh website paper audit.

caseEdges.label: E05
caseEdges.meaning: Transition from a uniform state to hexagonal and striped Turing patterns
caseEdges.support: A chemically supplied reaction–diffusion experiment produces stationary patterned states from a uniform regime.
caseEdges.supplied: Specific reactions, diffusion, gel geometry and reagent supply are provided.
caseEdges.limit: A stationary spatial mode is not automatically a temporal oscillation or a self-maintaining resonator. Uniform-state instability is not identical to noise-induced ordering.
caseEdges.locator: 06_evidence_catalog.md E05; original-paper location as reported there
caseEdges.readDepth: Source-reported 2026-10-02: Publisher abstract and bibliographic record. Not a fresh website paper audit.

caseEdges.label: E06
caseEdges.meaning: Resonant pattern formation in a chemical system
caseEdges.support: Periodic illumination of a photosensitive chemical oscillator locks responses to the forcing and changes the spatial pattern. External temporal forcing changes spatial patterns; H04 is context only, not measured mutual oscillator coupling.
caseEdges.supplied: The reaction medium and periodic optical drive are supplied externally.
caseEdges.limit: The experiment links temporal forcing and spatial organization, not the spontaneous origin of the drive or new fundamental laws.
caseEdges.locator: 06_evidence_catalog.md E06; original-paper location as reported there
caseEdges.readDepth: Source-reported 2026-10-02: Publisher abstract and record. Not a fresh website paper audit.

caseEdges.label: E07
caseEdges.meaning: Dicke quantum phase transition with a superfluid gas in an optical cavity
caseEdges.support: A pumped atom–cavity system undergoes a collective transition with mutually coupled matter organization and optical-field dynamics.
caseEdges.supplied: Atoms, cavity boundaries and laser pumping are given.
caseEdges.limit: This is a close geometry–field feedback example, but not unstructured matter producing its own complete apparatus or successive autonomous levels.
caseEdges.locator: Primary paper abstract: Dicke transition and atom–cavity self-organization; 06 E07.
caseEdges.readDepth: Source-reported 2026-10-02: Publisher abstract and article record. Not a fresh website paper audit.

caseEdges.label: E08
caseEdges.meaning: Tunable colloidal swarmalators with hydrodynamic coupling
caseEdges.support: Phase and arrangement co-evolve; the paper also reports synchronization-dependent lateral hydrodynamic forces (Figure 5e–f).
caseEdges.supplied: Feedback-controlled active particles and hydrodynamic interactions are part of the experimental mechanism.
caseEdges.limit: The control architecture is essential context; it cannot be omitted when describing how spontaneous the organization is.
caseEdges.locator: Primary paper pp. 5–6, hydrodynamic coupling and Figure 5e–f; 06 E08.
caseEdges.readDepth: Source-reported 2026-10-02: Publisher HTML, including setup/control description. Not a fresh website paper audit. Primary PDF relevant result/caption text inspected 5 October 2026; no figure/data analysis.

caseEdges.label: E09
caseEdges.meaning: Self-Organized Resonance during Search of a Diverse Chemical Space
caseEdges.support: A driven reacting-particle model develops structures matched to periodic forcing; in the studied regime their energy absorption helps stabilization.
caseEdges.supplied: Toy reaction rules, Brownian dynamics and a periodic drive are specified.
caseEdges.limit: This is not laboratory evidence and does not show that maximum absorption is a universal selection rule. Compare E17.
caseEdges.locator: 06_evidence_catalog.md E09; original-paper location as reported there
caseEdges.readDepth: Source-reported 2026-10-02: Original-paper abstract on APS and author-institution record. Not a fresh website paper audit.

caseEdges.label: E10
caseEdges.meaning: Experimental observation of self-replicating spots in a reaction–diffusion system
caseEdges.support: Chemical spots grow and split repeatedly in a laboratory reaction–diffusion system.
caseEdges.supplied: Reactive chemicals and nonequilibrium experimental conditions are supplied.
caseEdges.limit: Pattern duplication is not automatically reproduction with heredity, or a new organizational level. Do not infer a resonant microscopic mechanism merely from the shared shape of the process.
caseEdges.locator: 06_evidence_catalog.md E10; original-paper location as reported there
caseEdges.readDepth: Source-reported 2026-10-02: Publisher abstract and bibliographic record. Not a fresh website paper audit.

caseEdges.label: E11
caseEdges.meaning: Self-Replicating Holes in a Vertically Vibrated Dense Suspension
caseEdges.support: Holes in a vertically driven starch suspension deform and split under suitable forcing.
caseEdges.supplied: The suspension, container and sustained vertical vibration already exist.
caseEdges.limit: A hole is a spatial pattern in supplied material, not a newly manufactured independent resonator or organism. Shape instability is part of replication here.
caseEdges.locator: 06_evidence_catalog.md E11; original-paper location as reported there
caseEdges.readDepth: Source-reported 2026-10-02: Original-paper abstract on APS. Not a fresh website paper audit.

caseEdges.label: E12
caseEdges.meaning: Dynamic self-assembly of magnetized, millimetre-sized objects rotating at a liquid–air interface
caseEdges.support: Magnetically driven objects organize through their motion and fluid-mediated interactions.
caseEdges.supplied: Fabricated magnetic objects, liquid interface and rotating external field are provided.
caseEdges.limit: The result connects maintained activity and spatial arrangement. It does not imply all stable structures need continuous external driving.
caseEdges.locator: Primary paper abstract: rotating objects, fluid-mediated interactions and dynamic self-assembly; 06 E12.
caseEdges.readDepth: Source-reported 2026-10-02: Publisher abstract and bibliographic record. Not a fresh website paper audit.

caseEdges.label: E13
caseEdges.meaning: Spontaneous network formation among cooperative RNA replicators
caseEdges.support: RNA fragments assemble into catalytic networks; tested cooperative networks have growth advantages over competing autocatalytic cycles.
caseEdges.supplied: Selected RNA sequences, fragments and controlled chemical conditions are supplied.
caseEdges.limit: This supports chemical organizational feedback and cooperation, not an identical acoustic or fundamental-particle mechanism. A formal catalytic graph alone does not establish sustained kinetics.
caseEdges.locator: 06_evidence_catalog.md E13; original-paper location as reported there
caseEdges.readDepth: Source-reported 2026-10-02: Publisher abstract and change history; full subscription methods not inspected. Not a fresh website paper audit.

caseEdges.label: E14
caseEdges.meaning: Transport, Collective Motion, and Brownian Motion
caseEdges.support: Projection of many-body dynamics leads to a reduced description involving collective variables, memory and effective fluctuating forces.
caseEdges.supplied: Microscopic dynamics and a projection/choice of resolved variables are supplied.
caseEdges.limit: Unresolved dynamics need not be white noise. Describing a system at lower resolution does not physically create a new medium or hierarchy.
caseEdges.locator: 06_evidence_catalog.md E14; original-paper location as reported there
caseEdges.readDepth: Source-reported 2026-10-02: Original publisher abstract and record; historical derivation not independently re-proved. Not a fresh website paper audit.

caseEdges.label: E15
caseEdges.meaning: Realization of the Hofstadter Hamiltonian with Ultracold Atoms in Optical Lattices
caseEdges.support: Laser-assisted tunnelling implements an effective lattice Hamiltonian with magnetic-field-like phases.
caseEdges.supplied: Cold atoms, an optical lattice and precisely controlled driving are provided.
caseEdges.limit: This demonstrates selected effective dynamics, not arbitrary alteration of fundamental laws or a frequency-only recipe.
caseEdges.locator: 06_evidence_catalog.md E15; original-paper location as reported there
caseEdges.readDepth: Source-reported 2026-10-02: Original-paper abstract on APS. Not a fresh website paper audit.

caseEdges.label: E16
caseEdges.meaning: A colloidal viewpoint on the sausage catastrophe and the finite sphere packing problem
caseEdges.support: Confinement of colloidal spheres in vesicles influences which packing geometries occur, including competing arrangements.
caseEdges.supplied: Pre-existing particles, confining membranes and their material properties are provided.
caseEdges.limit: This is evidence that geometry affects accessible organization, not evidence that every such effect requires resonance.
caseEdges.locator: 06_evidence_catalog.md E16; original-paper location as reported there
caseEdges.readDepth: Source-reported 2026-10-02: Publisher HTML; not an independent reproduction of simulations. Not a fresh website paper audit.

caseEdges.label: E17
caseEdges.meaning: Drive-specific selection in multistable mechanical networks
caseEdges.resultType: simulation; published report also includes experimental evidence
caseEdges.support: In studied driven mechanical networks, selected configurations absorb relatively little work from the drive.
caseEdges.supplied: Multistable spring networks, their interaction landscape and an external drive are supplied.
caseEdges.limit: This constrains “strongest resonance always dominates”; it does not refute a conditional geometry–mode hypothesis. The experimental portion was not separately method-audited here.
caseEdges.locator: 06_evidence_catalog.md E17; original-paper location as reported there
caseEdges.readDepth: Source-reported 2026-10-02: Author preprint arXiv:1908.09332 plus journal metadata and original abstract indexed by PubMed. Not a fresh website paper audit.

caseEdges.label: E18
caseEdges.meaning: Optical binding
caseEdges.support: Illuminated microspheres display light-mediated interactions and bound configurations.
caseEdges.supplied: An external optical field, microspheres and surrounding medium already exist.
caseEdges.limit: Field scattering and particle arrangement interact, but a bound pair is not yet a recursively reproducing hierarchy.
caseEdges.locator: Primary paper abstract: optically induced binding of particles; 06 E18.
caseEdges.readDepth: Source-reported 2026-10-02: Original-paper abstract and record on APS. Not a fresh website paper audit.

caseEdges.label: E19
caseEdges.meaning: Controlling dispersion forces between small particles with artificially created random light fields
caseEdges.support: Artificially generated random light produces measured attractive interactions between dielectric microspheres. H01/H06 denote narrower imposed-background components, not support for the entire compound hypotheses.
caseEdges.supplied: Pre-existing spheres and a laser-generated, quasi-monochromatic random optical field are provided.
caseEdges.limit: Random does not mean broadband white noise. The experiment supports fluctuation-mediated interaction, not spontaneous creation of the spheres; broader interaction designs include theoretical proposals.
caseEdges.locator: Primary paper experimental random-light interaction results versus proposed interaction design; 06 E19.
caseEdges.readDepth: Source-reported 2026-10-02: Publisher HTML, including experimental versus theoretical scope. Not a fresh website paper audit.

caseEdges.label: E20
caseEdges.meaning: Self-replicating segregation patterns in horizontally vibrated binary mixture of granules
caseEdges.support: Driven granules form and split bands; collisions can annihilate them. Bands change surface-flow amplitudes, and parameter regimes also occur without bands.
caseEdges.supplied: Two grain populations, a container and continued horizontal shaking are supplied.
caseEdges.limit: This connects vibration, organization and pattern multiplication without biological copying machinery. It does not establish successive independent scales.
caseEdges.locator: Primary paper Results and Figures 2–5; 06 E20.
caseEdges.readDepth: Source-reported 2026-10-02: Publisher HTML. Supplementary materials were not independently reproduced. Not a fresh website paper audit. Primary PDF relevant result/caption text inspected 5 October 2026; no video/data analysis.

caseEdges.label: E21
caseEdges.meaning: Pattern formation in a Swift-Hohenberg equation with spatially periodic coefficients
caseEdges.support: A slow-amplitude description is justified for a specified pattern-forming equation near onset, under stated spectral and coefficient assumptions. H10/H11 are method context only, not physical creation of a medium.
caseEdges.supplied: The equation, spatially periodic coefficients and near-instability regime are specified.
caseEdges.limit: A controlled change of scale in description is not an unlimited sequence of new physical levels. The environmental heterogeneity is given, not derived from the emerging pattern.
caseEdges.locator: 06_evidence_catalog.md E21; original-paper location as reported there
caseEdges.readDepth: Source-reported 2026-10-02: Publisher HTML, including assumptions and approximation result. Not an independent formal proof check. Not a fresh website paper audit.

caseEdges.label: E22
caseEdges.meaning: Thermodynamics of bouncing grains
caseEdges.support: Grain transport is measured on a heterogeneous, nonresonating vibrating plate; effective statistical and transport descriptions are studied.
caseEdges.supplied: A driven plate, heterogeneity and grains are provided.
caseEdges.limit: Vibration-induced transport is not by itself proof of resonance. The earlier document incorrectly grouped this study as an unqualified resonant-mode example.
caseEdges.locator: 06_evidence_catalog.md E22; original-paper location as reported there
caseEdges.readDepth: Source-reported 2026-10-02: Original-paper abstract on APS; no raw-data reanalysis. Not a fresh website paper audit.

caseEdges.label: E01
caseEdges.meaning: Formation of optical supramolecular structures in a fibre laser by tailoring long-range soliton interactions
caseEdges.support: Pulse-generated acoustic attraction competes with dispersive-wave repulsion; nested assemblies contain single and bound soliton units. Pump perturbations can turn noise spikes into stable solitons incorporated into an existing assembly.
caseEdges.supplied: Designed, pumped fibre-laser system; optical molecules are bound pulses, not chemical molecules.
caseEdges.limit: Pulses drive an acoustic field that acts back on their interactions; smaller optical structures participate in a larger assembly. The designed pumped laser remains part of the system.
caseEdges.locator: Primary paper Results, Elementary diversity and addition/removal; Figures 1, 3, 5.
caseEdges.readDepth: Archived register dated 30 September 2026 reports: Full primary paper and supplementary text; Figure 3 inspected as a rendered page. This is retained earlier inspection, not a fresh full-paper review. Primary PDF result/caption text inspected 5 October 2026; no media/data replication.

caseEdges.edition: RRG v0.2 locked + evidence updates; promoted 2026-10-01
caseEdges.label: E02
caseEdges.meaning: Heteronuclear soliton molecules in optical microresonators
caseEdges.support: Pulses of different carrier frequencies and amplitudes coexist in a bound optical structure while their relative phase evolves.
caseEdges.supplied: Driven Kerr microresonator; distinguish carrier frequency from collective repetition rate.
caseEdges.limit: Different pulse properties can coexist within a bound structure; collective organization does not require all carriers to have identical phase.
caseEdges.locator: Introduction; Figures 1–4; electro-optic measurements and coupled Lugiato–Lefever modelling.
caseEdges.readDepth: Archived register dated 30 September 2026 reports: Full primary author manuscript, cross-checked against publisher record. This is retained earlier inspection, not a fresh full-paper review.

caseEdges.supplied: Reconstituted lipid/protein system with ATP; the simulation uses a phenomenological movement coupling.
caseEdges.limit: A protein–membrane feedback system supports persistent motion with supplied materials and ATP. Do not describe the simulated interruption of the loop as an experimental ablation.
caseEdges.locator: Primary Results on geometric cues; Figure 3; Extended Data Figure 6 (simulation).
caseEdges.readDepth: Archived register dated 30 September 2026 reports: Full primary article, methods and figure descriptions. This is retained earlier inspection, not a fresh full-paper review. Primary indexed publisher result/caption text inspected 5 October 2026; full Methods fetch unavailable.

caseEdges.label: E08
caseEdges.meaning: Dicke quantum phase transition with a superfluid gas in an optical cavity
caseEdges.resultType: Quantum-gas experiment with quantitative threshold comparison.
caseEdges.support: Atoms and a supplied cavity field self-organize through reciprocal feedback. This is exactly current 06 E07 / BIB-0036, not an extra confirmation.
caseEdges.supplied: Pumped atom–cavity system; its threshold equation is domain-specific.
